statusDetail: Coverage complete. Lighthouse and one HAR attempt encountered intermittent HTTP 503; first-party trace, raw CDP probes, screenshots, DOM, axe, headers, cookies, trackers, images, discoverability, and heap evidence completed all checks.

page.notes: Server-rendered adult media/listing site with localized domains, public listings, category pages, detail pages, consent overlay, manifest, and service worker.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshot and preference probe show a usable dark surface and authored prefers-color-scheme rules.
The preferences probe under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce found eight running shimmer-56cf2 animations, each with a 2000 ms duration.
axe-core reported 48 color-contrast nodes; the preference/CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule in accessible styles.
DOM/CSS inspection found no authored View Transition rules on the representative listing and detail routes, and route navigation performs full abrupt swaps.
No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface was present on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked animation or scrollytelling surface was present on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No swipe, pull, drag, or snap-based primary interaction was present on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No swipe, pull, drag, or snap-based primary interaction was present on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots show the same tall header and persistent 190 px sidebar; DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state-driven treatment.
Visible header/sidebar navigation remained attached without clipped transient overlays on all captured paths.
Active underline, headings, and persistent category navigation clearly indicate location on listing/category paths.
Desktop, categories, and detail screenshots all show a centered 525 px-wide consent overlay covering the page before interaction. Refuse is available, but the content remains obscured.
Recon found zero dialog or popover elements while the screenshot shows a modal-like blocking surface.
At 360 px, the 190 px sidebar plus clipped content and the full header leave roughly half the visual viewport for the feed.
Layout evidence reports 664 px horizontal overflow on both homepage and categories (scrollWidth 1024, visual viewport 360). The detail template lacks viewport meta and is scaled to 0.367.
The same desktop sidebar/content arrangement remains 1024 px wide on two narrow listing templates, clipping the content rather than adapting.
axe-core found an aria-hidden login section containing focusable content and one nested interactive control, both of which can disrupt keyboard and assistive-technology interaction.
Homepage and category screenshots have descriptive H1s and immediately visible linked media/cards.
A homepage content link resolved to a detail page with matching H1, title, creator, and primary viewing action.
HAR and direct fetch attempts received HTTP 503 responses containing only the stock nginx “Service Temporarily Unavailable” page; no retry, status, or navigation action was offered.
Trace measured FCP/LCP 1083.51 ms, TBT 116.17 ms; layout captures measured CLS 0.
Homepage and category layout observers recorded CLS 0 with no shift entries.
Trace found two long tasks, longest 157.86 ms, with 116.17 ms total blocking time, acceptable for this load.
The image audit found 29/36 homepage images and 28/32 detail images without explicit dimensions, 12 oversized homepage images, and multiple below-fold images without lazy loading.
The live tracker probe observed 139 resources from 15 origins, including 14 third-party origins and 81 requests to static-ah.xhcdn.com.
axe-core found prohibited ARIA on a video span, an aria-hidden region containing focusable content, and a nested interactive control.
axe-core reported 48 color-contrast failures across headings, active navigation, metadata, and consent text.
axe-core reported non-unique landmarks, a nested complementary landmark, seven regions outside landmarks, and focusable content inside aria-hidden UI.
Screenshots show readable text sizing and stable card-title wrapping, apart from separately reported contrast/reflow defects.
The detail layout reports hasViewportMeta=false and Chrome scales a 980 px layout to 0.367 on a 360 px device.
A five-second active error/unhandledrejection observer recorded zero runtime errors after load.
Image probes found dimensions missing on 29 of 36 homepage images and 28 of 32 detail images, with 12 homepage images over twice their display width.
No permission prompt appeared, Notification.permission remained default, and the representative paths completed without browser-blocking UI.
Homepage, category, and detail probes found unique descriptive titles and meta descriptions.
The mobile detail layout directly reports hasViewportMeta=false; the page renders as a 980 px desktop canvas scaled down.
Both in-page fetches returned HTTP 503 for /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml during the run, while the main document was otherwise reachable.
The detail probe found Open Graph metadata but zero application/ld+json scripts for a page representing a video entity.
CSP is only frame-ancestors self; three of four cookies were flagged insecure, including settings and x_csrf_token without Secure, and settings uses SameSite=None.
The tracker probe observed 14 third-party origins, including accounts.google.com, tsydicate.com, img.doppiocdn.com, multiple CDNs, and collection endpoints.
No notification permission was requested on load (permission remained default); authentication was not forced into the public browsing flow.
Headers evidence shows no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy, a narrow Permissions-Policy, CSP limited to frame-ancestors, and HSTS max-age of only 86400 seconds.
Discoverability evidence found 74% raw/rendered text overlap, title/H1/description in raw HTML, and no JS shell.
Three representative routes rendered stable navigation/content without cut-off overlays after load.
A valid manifest was fetched and an active service worker controlled the full origin scope.
The captured 503 response is a generic server page with no explanation, retry control, or preserved site navigation.
The document declares lang=fr and recon exposes localized alternate-domain links for dozens of languages including RTL languages.
The audited public paths display no dates, currencies, or locale-sensitive numeric input requiring formatting.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited public paths display no dates, currencies, or locale-sensitive numeric input requiring formatting.

Before/after heap summaries showed no Detached constructor among top retained classes after ten repeated toggles.

paths.description: Homepage/listing archetype and public content-discovery entry point; tested desktop, dark/reduced/contrast preferences, narrow mobile, performance, security, privacy, resilience, discoverability, and accessibility.
Category index archetype, representing dense taxonomy/listing pages and localized navigation.
Representative public video-detail archetype reached from the homepage, covering content metadata, primary viewing action, media assets, mobile behavior, and repeated interaction memory.
Authenticated watch history, subscriptions, creator upload, checkout, and account-management flows were not covered because they require account state and potentially consequential actions.

findings.summary: Loading shimmer animations continue when reduced motion is requested
findings.evidence: The preferences probe under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce found eight running shimmer-56cf2 animations, each with a 2000 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential shimmer and transition animations inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: The default palette has widespread contrast failures and no observed contrast-specific adaptation
findings.evidence: axe-core reported 48 color-contrast nodes; the preference/CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule in accessible styles.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the failing color pairs and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no authored View Transition rules on the representative listing and detail routes, and route navigation performs full abrupt swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for listing-to-detail navigation, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The large fixed navigation chrome does not adapt as users scroll
findings.evidence: Screenshots show the same tall header and persistent 190 px sidebar; DOM/CSS inspection found no scroll-state-driven treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries to compact or reveal persistent chrome according to scroll position.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the primary content on every fresh load
findings.evidence: Desktop, categories, and detail screenshots all show a centered 525 px-wide consent overlay covering the page before interaction. Refuse is available, but the content remains obscured.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep equal accept/refuse controls but present consent in a compact non-obscuring surface where legally possible.

findings.summary: The blocking consent overlay is not exposed as a native dialog
findings.evidence: Recon found zero dialog or popover elements while the screenshot shows a modal-like blocking surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the consent flow with a native <dialog> and declarative dismissal/focus behavior.

findings.summary: Persistent desktop chrome crowds out content on a narrow viewport
findings.evidence: At 360 px, the 190 px sidebar plus clipped content and the full header leave roughly half the visual viewport for the feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the desktop sidebar with compact mobile navigation and prioritize the content column.

findings.summary: Homepage and category templates force a 1024 px desktop layout into a 360 px viewport
findings.evidence: Layout evidence reports 664 px horizontal overflow on both homepage and categories (scrollWidth 1024, visual viewport 360). The detail template lacks viewport meta and is scaled to 0.367.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width on every template, remove fixed desktop minimum widths, and reflow navigation/cards at narrow sizes.

findings.summary: Reused listing/navigation components do not adapt to their available container
findings.evidence: The same desktop sidebar/content arrangement remains 1024 px wide on two narrow listing templates, clipping the content rather than adapting.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable navigation and card-grid components container-query breakpoints and intrinsic sizing.

findings.summary: Keyboard semantics and focus containment have serious defects
findings.evidence: axe-core found an aria-hidden login section containing focusable content and one nested interactive control, both of which can disrupt keyboard and assistive-technology interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove hidden descendants from the tab order, avoid nested controls, and verify visible :focus-visible states.

findings.summary: Server failures expose a generic dead end with no recovery action
findings.evidence: HAR and direct fetch attempts received HTTP 503 responses containing only the stock nginx “Service Temporarily Unavailable” page; no retry, status, or navigation action was offered.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded, accessible 503 state with retry, status information, and safe navigation back to available content.

findings.summary: Image delivery is inefficient across listing and detail templates
findings.evidence: The image audit found 29/36 homepage images and 28/32 detail images without explicit dimensions, 12 oversized homepage images, and multiple below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions, select right-sized responsive sources, lazy-load below-fold media, and prioritize only the LCP candidate.

findings.summary: A large third-party/request surface is loaded for the initial experience
findings.evidence: The live tracker probe observed 139 resources from 15 origins, including 14 third-party origins and 81 requests to static-ah.xhcdn.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit initial-route dependencies, remove duplicate/nonessential integrations, and conditionally load third-party features on demand.

findings.summary: ARIA role/name semantics contain serious violations
findings.evidence: axe-core found prohibited ARIA on a video span, an aria-hidden region containing focusable content, and a nested interactive control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native elements and valid ARIA, remove focusable descendants from aria-hidden content, and unnest interactive controls.

findings.summary: Text and controls fail WCAG AA contrast at scale
findings.evidence: axe-core reported 48 color-contrast failures across headings, active navigation, metadata, and consent text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state, then rerun axe and visual checks.

findings.summary: Landmark and focus structure is not robust
findings.evidence: axe-core reported non-unique landmarks, a nested complementary landmark, seven regions outside landmarks, and focusable content inside aria-hidden UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use unique labelled landmarks, keep asides top-level, contain content in landmarks, and repair hidden focus handling.

findings.summary: The detail page prevents proper mobile reflow by omitting viewport metadata
findings.evidence: The detail layout reports hasViewportMeta=false and Chrome scales a 980 px layout to 0.367 on a 360 px device.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 to every template and ensure content reflows at 320 CSS px and zoom.

findings.summary: Most content images omit intrinsic dimensions and several are oversized
findings.evidence: Image probes found dimensions missing on 29 of 36 homepage images and 28 of 32 detail images, with 12 homepage images over twice their display width.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio and correctly sized responsive image candidates.

findings.summary: The public video-detail template has no viewport meta tag
findings.evidence: The mobile detail layout directly reports hasViewportMeta=false; the page renders as a 980 px desktop canvas scaled down.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a viewport meta tag to the shared detail-page head and verify mobile rendering.

findings.summary: robots.txt and sitemap.xml were intermittently unavailable
findings.evidence: Both in-page fetches returned HTTP 503 for /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml during the run, while the main document was otherwise reachable.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep robots and sitemap endpoints highly available and outside aggressive rate limiting; monitor them separately.

findings.summary: The video detail has social tags but no structured VideoObject data
findings.evidence: The detail probe found Open Graph metadata but zero application/ld+json scripts for a page representing a video entity.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD matching the visible title, thumbnail, duration, upload date, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but XSS/header protection and cookie flags are weak
findings.evidence: CSP is only frame-ancestors self; three of four cookies were flagged insecure, including settings and x_csrf_token without Secure, and settings uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on all HTTPS cookies, review SameSite, and deploy an enforceable script/style CSP with nonces or hashes.

findings.summary: The initial page contacts a broad third-party surface
findings.evidence: The tracker probe observed 14 third-party origins, including accounts.google.com, tsydicate.com, img.doppiocdn.com, multiple CDNs, and collection endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory every origin, defer optional integrations until consent/intent, proxy where appropriate, and remove low-value calls.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent or too weak
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy, a narrow Permissions-Policy, CSP limited to frame-ancestors, and HSTS max-age of only 86400 seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff and a strict Referrer-Policy, tighten Permissions-Policy, strengthen CSP, and extend HSTS after deployment validation.

findings.summary: Network/server failure handling falls back to an unhelpful nginx page
findings.evidence: The captured 503 response is a generic server page with no explanation, retry control, or preserved site navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle 5xx responses at the application/edge layer with an accessible recoverable fallback and retry path.

findings.summary: Image bytes and formats are not consistently matched to rendered size
findings.evidence: The homepage image probe found 12 oversized images and 17 legacy-format resources; detail found two oversized and 18 legacy-format resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve modern negotiated formats and width-based responsive candidates sized close to their rendered slots.

findings.summary: The initial route performs a high volume of distributed network work
findings.evidence: The page recorded 139 resource entries and 14 third-party origins before user interaction, with one CDN alone receiving 81 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-visible and optional modules, consolidate requests, and pause background work when content is off-screen.

findings.summary: Third-party integrations are disproportionate on the first view
findings.evidence: Fourteen third-party origins are contacted during initial load, before the user selects a media item; this adds connection and processing overhead.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, load integrations only after intent/consent, and regularly remove origins that do not justify their cost.

taskList.title: Rebuild narrow-screen layout and restore viewport metadata
Repair contrast, ARIA, landmarks, and keyboard focus
Harden CSP, cookies, and defensive headers
Add recoverable 5xx handling and protect crawler endpoints
Reduce and defer the third-party/request footprint
Replace the consent overlay with semantic, less-obscuring UI
Respect reduced motion and add progressive route transitions
Make persistent chrome react to scroll position
